title: Secure a loose trouser hem
instruction: Secure the loose trouser hem with the safety pin, with its point safely enclosed.
setup: An inside-out cotton trouser cuff, 180 mm across and 240 mm long, rests over a 140 x 190 x 100 mm wooden sewing support inserted between its faces. The 20 mm turned front hem overhangs the support by 46 mm toward the left arm; its middle 100 mm of stitching is loose. The back stays below the support. An ordinary 75 mm steel safety pin lies open toward the right arm. Both hands start open.
scoring: 1.0 if the pin passes through both front and hem layers within the loose central 100 mm, returns through them to the surface, and closes with its point inside the shield; the hem remains secured after a three-second release. 0.5 if both layers are threaded but the pin is still open or held; 0.25 if a correct layer remains partly threaded on the shaft. Otherwise 0. Pinning outside that loose section or through the back of the leg, more than four punctures, or a tear over 5 mm scores 0.
fidelity: Native cloth panels, sprung pin and finger contacts. A disclosed 0.02 N contact gate creates sliding holes at the loaded needle point; it is not calibrated puncture strength. Closing must overcome the spring and enclose the point. Material, contact and regularized slender-body inertias are approximate. No hand attachment or commanded prop motion. Full native feasibility remains pending.
context: A safety pin can hold a loose turned trouser hem until it can be sewn properly.
reset_notes: Use a cotton-twill trouser cuff with a 20 mm factory crease; unpick the securing thread from a 100 mm front section and remove loose thread. Replace punctured fabric after each trial. Restore the photographed fold, inspect the pin and protective pad covers, and leave the pin open.
